environment.description: Same Flask application deployed in a hardened configuration. The ECS task definition specifies a read-only root filesystem with the SQLite database mounted as a read-only bind from EFS with access point enforcement (uid:gid 1000:1000, read-only POSIX permissions 0444). The container runs with a custom seccomp profile that restricts syscalls to a baseline set. Additionally, the EFS access point is configured with an IAM authorization policy requiring the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action which is explicitly denied in the task role's permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/DenyEFSWrite). The SQLite database is opened in WAL mode with journal_mode=WAL and the connection uses the query parameter '?mode=ro' in the URI, but the critical control is the filesystem-level read-only enforcement.

config.compute: ECS Fargate, Python 3.11, Flask 2.3, readonlyRootFilesystem: true
config.database: SQLite on EFS access point (read-only POSIX 0444, enforced uid/gid)

efs_access_point.policy: elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite explicitly denied in task role permission boundary

config.seccomp_profile: blocks fchmod, fchown, chmod, chown, rename, unlink, truncate
